fixtures.title: Attention-only sequence transduction (Transformer)
fixtures.source: Original summary written for this repository of Vaswani et al., 2017 (arXiv:1706.03762); not the paper's text.
fixtures.text: We propose a sequence transduction model based solely on attention, the Transformer, which dispenses with recurrence and convolutions. Multi-head attention lets the model attend to information from different representation subspaces. Because the model has no recurrence, positional encoding injects token order. Each layer also contains a feed forward network, residual connections and layer normalization. Self-attention connects all positions in a constant number of steps. Training uses the Adam optimizer and dropout, and a softmax output gives probabilities over the vocabulary.

fixtures.title: Low-rank adaptation of language models
fixtures.source: Original summary written for this repository of Hu et al., 2021 (arXiv:2106.09685); not the paper's text.
fixtures.text: Adapting a large language model (LLM) to each task by full fine-tuning is costly. We freeze the pretrained weights and train a low-rank update to each weight matrix, a method we call low-rank adaptation (LoRA). This parameter-efficient fine-tuning needs far fewer trainable parameters and adds no inference latency. We apply it to the attention weights of a Transformer and train with gradient descent and the Adam optimizer. Overfitting is limited by the small number of trainable parameters.

fixtures.title: Aligning a language model with human feedback
fixtures.source: Original summary written for this repository, in the spirit of Ouyang et al., 2022 (arXiv:2203.02155) and Schulman et al., 2017 (arXiv:1707.06347); not their text.
fixtures.text: We fine-tune a language model with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). Human comparisons train a reward model. The policy is then optimised with proximal policy optimization (PPO), a policy gradient method whose clipped objective keeps updates small. The task is a Markov decision process in which each generated token is an action, and a value function estimates the expected reward.

fixtures.title: Graph attention networks
fixtures.source: Original summary written for this repository of Velickovic et al., 2018 (arXiv:1710.10903); not the paper's text.
fixtures.text: We present graph attention networks (GATs), neural network architectures for graph-structured data. Each node attends over its neighbours with masked self-attention, a form of message passing, so no costly matrix operation or knowledge of the graph structure is needed. The layers are trained with backpropagation and dropout. Compared with a graph convolutional network, a GAT assigns different importance to different neighbours.

fixtures.title: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models
fixtures.source: Original summary written for this repository of Ho et al., 2020 (arXiv:2006.11239); not the paper's text.
fixtures.text: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models generate images by reversing a gradual noising process. The forward process adds Gaussian noise according to a noise schedule, and the reverse process is learned by a neural network, a U-Net, that predicts the noise. Training optimises a variational bound related to score matching. We report sample quality on image datasets.

fixtures.title: Thermal conductivity of graphene nanoribbons
fixtures.source: Original text written for this repository as an out-of-scope negative example.
fixtures.text: We study the thermal conductivity of graphene nanoribbons using molecular dynamics. Heat flux is computed from atomic trajectories at several temperatures, and the results agree with experiment.
